reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it focuses on the breadth of Canadian bank fees and criticizes the banking-fee system. Although Coinbase branding appears, the material does not present a specific financial product, return claim, payment flow, or condition for viewers, and it is described as informational rather than investment advice.

opening.argument: The video pairs a financial-fee discussion with an explicit viewer action: the description says, "Subscribe to our channel here" and supplies a channel URL, while also attaching "#coinbase #Crypto #Blockchain." The closing frame prominently displays Coinbase, and the description contains Coinbase-specific financial disclaimers. That combination can function as a funnel toward a branded crypto ecosystem, even though the material does not state a token purchase or promised return. The evidence therefore supports concern about promotion connected to viewer engagement, with the exact participation or purchase pathway left unstated.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense treats the subject as purely fee education, but it does not explain why the description includes a subscription URL alongside crypto hashtags or why Coinbase is prominently shown at the end. Its disclaimer establishes only how the content is characterized; it does not rule out branded promotion or a viewer funnel. The absence of an explicit deposit instruction does not eliminate the promotional signal.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The subscription request is only a request to follow the channel, not an instruction to buy a token or transfer funds. The supplied text never links subscribing to appreciation, dividends, or any other financial benefit. The description expressly says the content is informational and does not recommend buying, selling, or holding a financial product.

opening.argument: Several genuine risk signals appear together: the description uses "#coinbase #Crypto #Blockchain," directs viewers to an external channel URL, and the final frame displays Coinbase branding. Those signals occur in a video framed around costly banking practices, which can make an alternative financial brand appear especially attractive by contrast. The record does not show a return promise or purchase instruction, so this is not proof of a token scheme; however, the crypto branding and external engagement path leave open a promotional token-related purpose that the educational framing does not fully dispel.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense acknowledges Coinbase branding but minimizes its significance. The combination of a crypto hashtag cluster, a subscription URL, and an end-card brand is more than evidence about bank fees alone. Calling the content informational does not negate the possibility that the surrounding presentation steers viewers toward Coinbase-related participation. The defense also relies on missing proof of a return, whereas the relevant concern is whether the signals create a promotional pathway.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These are contextual branding signals, not evidence of token acquisition or appreciation. The title identifies the subject as Canadian bank fees, and the transcript lists fee types rather than crypto assets or returns. The disclaimer specifically denies a recommendation to buy, sell, or hold a financial product, so the alleged token-related purpose is speculative.

opening.argument: Although the video adopts the appearance of a bank-fee explainer, its presentation can also be read as brand promotion. The on-screen message says "IT’S TIME TO UPDATE," the description asks viewers to subscribe through a channel link, and the closing frame centers Coinbase while the description associates the video with crypto and blockchain. In that context, criticism of bank fees may steer viewers away from traditional banking and toward a branded crypto alternative. The evidence does not establish a specific token or promised gain, but it supports the narrower concern that educational framing is being used to promote crypto participation.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the material criticism of fees, but that framing may be precisely what makes the branding persuasive: viewers are shown extensive fee complaints and then Coinbase appears as the prominent closing identity. The description also combines the message with crypto and blockchain hashtags and a subscription path. A disclaimer about investment advice does not answer whether the overall presentation promotes a crypto brand.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The bank-fee framing is supported directly by the title and transcript, not merely a cover story: the title names Canadian bank fees and the speaker enumerates fee categories. "IT’S TIME TO UPDATE" calls for system change, not crypto investment. Coinbase branding and hashtags do not show that viewers were steered to buy tokens, receive gains, or participate financially.
